svg.title: Executing an ADG: statuses over time
svg.desc: The status life cycle (staged, enqueued, finished) and five snapshots of the example ADG being dispatched, with each robot's command queue and the rule that let each action through.
svg.metadata: ["t = 0 start. a\u00b9\u2081 and a\u00b3\u2081 have no predecessors: sent at once. a\u00b9\u2082 waits: its Type 2 predecessor a\u00b3\u2081 is not finished.", "AGV 3 reports a\u00b3\u2081 done. a\u00b9\u2082 is sent: a\u00b9\u2081 (Type 1) is only enqueued, which is enough; a\u00b3\u2081 (Type 2) is finished. It queues behind a\u00b9\u2081.", "AGV 1 reports a\u00b9\u2081 done. AGV 1 starts a\u00b9\u2082 from its own queue; the dispatcher does nothing.", "AGV 1 reports a\u00b9\u2082 done. a\u00b2\u2081 is sent (its Type 2 predecessor a\u00b9\u2082 is finished), and a\u00b2\u2082 with it (Type 1 predecessor enqueued).", "AGV 2 reports a\u00b2\u2081, a\u00b2\u2082 done. All finished. Each robot drove as fast as it could; only the order was enforced."]

g.text: Enqueue rule: the previous action of the same robot (Type 1) is enqueued or finished, AND every action of another robot it depends on (Type 2) is finished.

g.text: Enqueue rule from Hönig et al., RA-L 2019. The ActionNode status names are the closest fields in interfaces/msg/ActionNode.msg; how the dispatcher maps them is not in the snapshots.

g.text: The dispatcher sends an action when its rule holds; the robot runs its queue in order and reports each completion; each report may release more actions.
